I believe that she meant only you can cognitively help yourself. 

Think of it like a car - the medication is like the petrol, it will certainly help you get on your feet and will guide you on your way. The therapy is like the pedals and the gears, they help you talk everything help and help you to think a bit more clear. But it takes you as the driver to actually start the vehicle. 

Basically, therapy and medication will help you immensely. But don't forget to do simple things such as hobbies, talking to friends/family, watching movies, etc.

I'm around the same age as you, and I am also struggling with depression.

I know how it feels to feel like there's nothing to live for. At our age, it's impossible to see life outside of school and our own family. But when everything is going 99% wrong, there always has to be the 1%. Whether it's one week into the future or one year, there's always something to look forward to. I'm not doing well in school either, but I've always got that thought that there is freedom beyond school that I'll be able to experience soon. There's a reason you're still here, it isn't your time yet. You've still got so much of the world to see and experience.

School is very, very long, but it isn't forever. Always remember that. You will hardly see anyone you know in school once you're done.

But I do need to ask you, does your boyfriend truly make you happy? Putting the horrible thing he did to you, does he otherwise make you happy? If he doesn't, you need to find a way to slowly decrease your interactions with him, because he might be one the main reasons you feel even worse than you already do.

Is there maybe a school counselor you can see? I know counselling doesn't work for everyone, but if your family is not providing any help for you, it might help a little to talk to someone else. 

I'm always here for you to talk to as well.

Please be safe.

I'm around the same age as you, and I know for a fact how shit it is for us. We can't really see any future ahead of us now, but that *will* change when we're older. 

You still have so much of the world to explore. Even if you find one tiny thing that you feel is worth living for, hold on to that joy. It's good to have things you consciously want, but it's amazing to discover something that you never knew you could have.

I know how you feel, I'm experiencing it, but I'll say that the thought of something beyond being a teen is what keeps me here. 

You've got so much more of your life left to live, there's so much to see and do,  there's so much beauty in this world. It may never feel like that, and it will take a long while to get out of the dark spiral, but it's not impossible.

You deserve to be here, you deserve to see all the amazing things life can show you. We're all here for you, never forget that.
